ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: After soybean protein is acted on by enzymes in the digestive tract in the human body, small peptides (short peptide chains) can be formed. Answer the question: The codons for some amino acids are shown in the table. If the coding sequence corresponding to a small peptide from soybean is UACGAACAUUGG, what is the amino acid sequence of this small peptide?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a two-column table. The header of the left column is “amino acid”, and the header of the right column is “codon”. The table shows: tryptophan corresponds to UGG; glutamic acid corresponds to GAA, GAG; tyrosine corresponds to UAC, UAU; histidine corresponds to CAU, CAC. Then reason: The coding sequence given in the question stem is UACGAACAUUGG. In the genetic code, every 3 bases form one codon, so from left to right it is divided into UAC, GAA, CAU, UGG. Looking up the table shows: UAC corresponds to tyrosine, GAA corresponds to glutamic acid, CAU corresponds to histidine, and UGG corresponds to tryptophan. Therefore, the amino acid sequence of this small peptide is tyrosine-glutamic acid-histidine-tryptophan.
